proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. Set m = floor(x). By definition of the floor function, m is an integer and m <= x < m + 1. Define f = x - m. Then f >= 0 because x >= m, and f < 1 because x < m + 1. Also, by the definition of fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m = f. Hence x = m + f = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real x.
solver_summary: Use the defining property of floor to write x = floor(x) + (x - floor(x)), and note that the remainder lies in [0,1).
vetter_reason: The proof exactly matches the lemma statement: for arbitrary real x, it defines m = floor(x) and f = x - m, then verifies m is an integer, x = m + f, and 0 <= f < 1. This is the standard floor/fractional-part decomposition and is complete with no semantic drift.
